title: Limits and continuity: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Limits and continuity: Visual Guide

1. Value Versus Approach | five functions sampled from both sides of x = 2 as the approach distance h shrinks, with an extra off-grid probe that catches a table of round numbers lying | the limit reads the neighbourhood and never consults f(2), so it can exist where the function is undefined, disagree with a value that is defined, or fail outright because the two one-sided limits disagree

2. Clearing 0/0 | six limits shown as the raw quotient beside the factored or conjugated form with the algebra worked line by line, plus a slider on c in (x^2 - c)/(x - 3) | direct substitution is legal exactly when the function is continuous there, and 0/0 only means the algebra is unfinished - factor a polynomial, conjugate a radical, and a finite limit forces the numerator to vanish too

3. Squeeze The Oscillation | four functions drawn inside their bounding pair while the window zooms toward the limit point, with the live band width | the two bounds must share one limit for the theorem to conclude anything, so bounded times vanishing is pinned to 0 while sin(1/x) trapped between -1 and 1 is not

4. Small Angle Ratios | the cos(x) < sin(x)/x < 1 squeeze tightening as x shrinks, then seven trigonometric limits with k and m sliders on the arguments | sin(x)/x -> 1 and (1 - cos x)/x^2 -> 1/2 generate all the rest, and forcing each argument to match its denominator leaves only the ratio of the arguments standing

5. Breaks And Skipped Values | five functions on [0, 4] classified from their left limit, right limit and f(2), with a draggable target line N, a live IVT hypothesis check and the real number of solutions | the taxonomy of discontinuities falls straight out of those three numbers, and one break lets a function skip an intermediate value - which is why the IVT demands continuity on a closed interval and promises existence only, never a count
